messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Japanese, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement (Japanese morphosyntax) | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------| | **Nel** | “in the middle of” – locative prepositional phrase introducing the central point | Use the locative particle **で** after a noun phrase denoting “midway” (e.g., **人生の途中で**). **Back‑translation:** “midway (of life)‑LOC”. | | **mezzo** | The central point of a span; here the midpoint of life’s journey | Render as the noun **途中** (“mid‑point”) modified by **の** to link to **人生**. **Back‑translation:** “midway”. | | **del** | Genitive linking “road” to the larger context (“of the”) | Use the genitive particle **の** to connect **道** to **人生** (e.g., **人生の道**). **Back‑translation:** “road‑GEN of life”. | | **cammin** | The route or way that one travels on; metaphor for life’s course | Translate as **道** (noun). Mark as the head of the noun phrase. **Back‑translation:** “road”. | | **di** | Marks possession/association between “road” and “our life” | Use **の** to link **道** to **我々の人生** (e.g., **我々の人生の道**). **Back‑translation:** “road‑GEN of our life”. | | **nostra** | Belonging to the speaker and companions; collective ownership of life | Render as the possessive adjective **我々の** (or **私たちの**) preceding **人生**. **Back‑translation:** “our”. | | **vita** | The span of existence of the speaker; the overall journey | Translate as **人生** (noun). **Back‑translation:** “life”. | | **mi** | Reflexive pronoun, 1st‑person singular (object) | Use the reflexive pronoun **自分を** or the verb‑internal reflexive **自分で** depending on the verb; here attach to **見つけた** as **自分を**. **Back‑translation:** “myself”. | | **ritrovai** | “found” – act of discovering or realizing one’s own state (simple past) | Use the past form of **見つける** → **見つけた** (or **見出した**). No tense‑aspect ambiguity. **Back‑translation:** “found”. | | **per** | Indicates interior location inside something (“within”) | Use the locative particle **で** after the noun phrase **暗い森** (e.g., **暗い森で**). **Back‑translation:** “within”. | | **una** | Indefinite article “a” (non‑specific noun) | Japanese does not mark indefiniteness; omit article but keep noun singular. **Back‑translation:** (none). | | **selva** | A densely wooded area; metaphorically dark and confusing | Translate as **森** (noun). Add adjective **暗い** for “dark”. **Back‑translation:** “forest”. | | **oscura** | Lacking light; conveys gloom and uncertainty | Render as the i‑adjective **暗い** modifying **森**. **Back‑translation:** “dark”. | | **ché** | Conjunction “for” introducing a causal clause | Use the causal conjunction **ので** or **から** after the preceding clause (e.g., **…から**). **Back‑translation:** “because”. | | **la** | Definite article “the” (specifies particular way) | Japanese omits articles; rely on context. **Back‑translation:** (none). | | **diritta** | Correct or proper; the morally/technically correct path | Translate as **正しい** (i‑adjective) modifying **道**. **Back‑translation:** “right”. | | **via** | The correct route or method of proceeding (noun) | Render as **道** (noun). **Back‑translation:** “way”. | | **era** | Past state of being; auxiliary for passive construction | Use the past copula **だった** after the noun phrase **正しい道**. **Back‑translation:** “was”. | | **smarrita** | State of being lost or not found; the correct way is absent | Use the past participial adjective **失われた** (or **見失われた**) modifying **道**. **Back‑translation:** “lost”. |
*Comparative direction*: No comparative or degree constructions appear; therefore no comparative direction is required (N/A).

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Japanese components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.
- Line 1: 人生の途中で / 人生の半ばで / 人生の中ほどで - Line 2: 暗い森の中で自分を見つけた / 暗い森に自分を見出した / 暗い森で自分を発見した - Line 3: 正しい道は失われていた / 正しい道が見失われていた / 正しい道は失くされていた

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Japanese lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 1 Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita
**Line Inventory:** - 人生の途中で
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already satisfies the “midway” sense and the implicit “road of life” metaphor.
**Target Text:** 人生の途中で
---
**Source Line:** 2 mi ritrovai per una selva oscura,
**Line Inventory:** - 暗い森の中で自分を見つけた
**Assembly Notes:** - Added the causal particle **から** after the phrase to link to the next line (function‑word only).
**Target Text:** 暗い森の中で自分を見つけたから,
---
**Source Line:** 3 ché la diritta via era smarrita.
**Line Inventory:** - 正しい道は失われていた
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra content added; the phrase expresses the lost “right way”.
**Target Text:** 正しい道は失われていた.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Japanese text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 1 - Target Text (from Step 4): 人生の途中で - Back-Translation (literal): midway in life - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Midway upon the road of our life - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 2 - Target Text (from Step 4): 暗い森の中で自分を見つけたから, - Back-Translation (literal): because I found myself in a dark forest , - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I found myself within a dark wood, - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: 暗い森の中で自分を見つけた,
- Line #: 3 - Target Text (from Step 4): 正しい道は失われていた. - Back-Translation (literal): the correct way was lost. - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): for the right way had been missed. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**UNVERIFIED** – Failing Line #: 2
```text 人生の途中で 暗い森の中で自分を見つけた, 正しい道は失われていた. ```
